spot.html_text: With respect to gastruloids and synthetic embryos (if the latter are successfully produced with human stem cells), the central question is whether these entities are sufficiently like human embryos in their structure and functions to give rise to moral concerns about their use in research. Gastruloids do not possess all the characteristics of an embryo, as they do not form all of the embryonic tissues (e.g., they do not have the trophectoderm, which mediates the attachment to the uterus).
